originality.rationale: The claim concerns the ultra-log-concavity of a dependent difference of discrete-uniform extreme order statistics, quantified by an all-alphabet sufficient sample bound and an exact six-face reversal. Targeted public-literature queries, relevant full article material, record retrieval and comparisons to available prior research did not identify an equivalent or implied statement. The 2023 theorem preserves ULC of individual order statistics only when the parent is ULC. A nondegenerate discrete-uniform parent is not ULC, and the dependent range is not an individual order statistic. Closest range work addresses expected values, correlation or a different geometric parent; none gives this count-shape theorem. Residual full-text and indexing risks are explicitly stated.
residual_risks: No exhaustive search of all print books or unindexed classical order-statistic notes is possible.

value.rationale: This is a motivated strong-shape emergence question for a natural dispersion statistic built from two dependent extreme order statistics of a discrete-uniform parent, which itself is not ultra-log-concave. The result establishes non-ULC of all two-draw ranges with >=4 faces, eventual strict ULC with an explicit sample-size bound for all finite alphabets, and the exact sharp threshold for the canonical six-faced die. These complementary boundaries demonstrate unexpected emergence of a strong mass-shape property and give shape control potentially useful for concentration and count-inference calculations. This is more than a known pmf-table recomputation; the infinite family conclusion and sharp nondegenerate die classification require independent proofs.
